   178→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   179→# Helpers for sync_triage_needed
   180→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   181→
   182→def _open_review_issue_ids(state: StateModel) -> set[str]:
   183→    """Return set of open issue IDs whose detector is 'review' or 'concerns'."""
   184→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   185→    return {
   186→        fid for fid, f in issues.items()
   187→        if f.get("status") == "open"
   188→        and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   189→    }
   190→
   191→
   192→def _new_review_ids_since_triage(
   193→    state: StateModel,
   194→    meta: dict,
   195→) -> set[str]:
   196→    """Return review issue IDs that are new since the last triage."""
   197→    current_review_ids = _open_review_issue_ids(state)
   198→    triaged_ids = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", []))
   199→    return current_review_ids - triaged_ids
   200→
   201→
   202→def _prune_all_triage_stages(order: list[str]) -> None:
   203→    """Remove all ``triage::*`` stage IDs from *order*."""
   204→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
   205→        while sid in order:
   206→            order.remove(sid)
   207→
   208→
   209→def _inject_pending_triage_stages(
   210→    order: list[str],
   211→    plan: PlanModel,
   212→    confirmed: set[str],
   213→) -> bool:
   214→    """Inject triage stages for pending (unconfirmed) items.
   215→
   216→    Returns True if any stages were injected.
   217→    """
   218→    insert_at = promoted_insertion_index(order, plan)
   219→    stage_names = ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "enrich", "sense-check", "commit")
   220→    existing = set(order)
   221→    injected_count = 0
   222→    for sid, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names, strict=False):
   223→        if name not in confirmed and sid not in existing:
   224→            order.insert(insert_at + injected_count, sid)
   225→            injected_count += 1
   226→    return injected_count > 0
   227→

   229→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   230→# Unscored dimension sync (front of queue, unconditional)
   231→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   232→
   233→def sync_unscored_dimensions(
   234→    plan: PlanModel,
   235→    state: StateModel,
   236→) -> UnscoredDimensionSyncResult:
   237→    """Keep the plan queue in sync with unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions.
   238→
   239→    1. **Prune** — remove ``subjective::*`` IDs from ``queue_order`` that are
   240→       no longer unscored AND not stale (avoids pruning stale IDs — that is
   241→       ``sync_stale_dimensions``' responsibility).
   242→    2. **Inject** — unconditionally prepend currently-unscored IDs to the
   243→       *front* of ``queue_order`` so initial reviews are the first priority.
   244→    """
   245→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   246→    result = UnscoredDimensionSyncResult()
   247→
   248→    # Mid-cycle: don't inject unscored dimensions — they'll surface at cycle end.
   249→    if plan.get("plan_start_scores"):
   250→        return result
   251→
   252→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   253→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   254→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   255→
   256→    # --- Cleanup: prune subjective IDs that are no longer unscored --------
   257→    # Only prune IDs that are neither unscored nor stale (stale sync owns those).
   258→    _prune_subjective_ids(order, keep_ids=unscored_ids | stale_ids, pruned=result.pruned)
   259→
   260→    # --- Inject: prepend unscored IDs after any promoted items -------------
   261→    _inject_subjective_ids(order, plan, inject_ids=unscored_ids, to_front=True, injected=result.injected)
   262→
   263→    return result
   264→
   265→
   266→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   267→# Stale dimension sync (back of queue, conditional)
   268→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   269→
   270→def sync_stale_dimensions(
   271→    plan: PlanModel,
   272→    state: StateModel,
   273→    *,
   274→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   275→    cycle_just_completed: bool = False,
   276→) -> StaleDimensionSyncResult:
   277→    """Keep the plan queue in sync with stale and under-target subjective dimensions.
   278→
   279→    1. Remove any ``subjective::*`` IDs from ``queue_order`` that are no
   280→       longer stale/under-target and not unscored (avoids pruning IDs owned
   281→       by ``sync_unscored_dimensions``).
   282→    2. Inject stale and under-target dimension IDs when either:
   283→       a. No objective items remain (mid-cycle: append to back), OR
   284→       b. A cycle just completed (post-cycle: insert at front so subjective
   285→          review takes priority over new objective issues).
   286→    """
   287→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   288→    result = StaleDimensionSyncResult()
   289→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   290→    under_target_ids = current_under_target_ids(state)
   291→    injectable_ids = stale_ids | under_target_ids
   292→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   293→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   294→
   295→    # --- Cleanup: prune resolved subjective IDs --------------------------
   296→    # Only prune IDs that are no longer injectable and not unscored.
   297→    _prune_subjective_ids(order, keep_ids=injectable_ids | unscored_ids, pruned=result.pruned)
   298→
   299→    # --- Inject or evict stale + under-target dimensions -----------------
   300→    has_real_items = _has_objective_backlog(state, policy)
   301→    should_inject = not has_real_items or cycle_just_completed
   302→
   303→    if not should_inject:
   304→        # Mid-cycle with objective backlog: evict any stale/under-target IDs
   305→        # that are present in the queue.  They may have been grandfathered from
   306→        # the unscored phase and should not be visible until the objective
   307→        # backlog clears or a cycle completes.
   308→        to_evict = [
   309→            fid for fid in order
   310→            if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   311→            and fid in injectable_ids
   312→        ]
   313→        for fid in to_evict:
   314→            order.remove(fid)
   315→            result.pruned.append(fid)
   316→
   317→    if should_inject and injectable_ids:
   318→        to_front = cycle_just_completed and has_real_items
   319→        _inject_subjective_ids(order, plan, inject_ids=injectable_ids, to_front=to_front, injected=result.injected)
   320→
   321→    return result
   322→

   324→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   325→# Triage snapshot hash + sync
   326→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   327→
   328→def review_issue_snapshot_hash(state: StateModel) -> str:
   329→    """Hash open review issue IDs to detect changes.
   330→
   331→    Returns empty string when there are no open review issues.
   332→    """
   333→    return stale_policy_mod.review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   334→
   335→
   336→@dataclass
   337→class TriageSyncResult:
   338→    """What changed during a triage sync."""
   339→
   340→    injected: bool = False
   341→    pruned: bool = False
   342→
   343→    @property
   344→    def changes(self) -> int:
   345→        return int(self.injected) + int(self.pruned)

   347→
   348→def sync_triage_needed(
   349→    plan: PlanModel,
   350→    state: StateModel,
   351→) -> TriageSyncResult:
   352→    """Inject 4 triage stage IDs at front of queue when review issues change.
   353→
   354→    Only injects stages not already confirmed in ``epic_triage_meta``.
   355→
   356→    When stages are already present but all new issues have been resolved
   357→    since injection, auto-prunes the stale stages and updates the hash.
   358→
   359→    When issues are *resolved* (current IDs are a subset of previously
   360→    triaged IDs), the snapshot hash is updated silently — no re-triage
   361→    is needed since the user is working through the plan.
   362→    """
   363→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   364→    result = TriageSyncResult()
   365→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   366→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   367→    confirmed = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   368→

   370→    already_present = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
   371→

   373→    last_hash = meta.get("issue_snapshot_hash", "")
   374→
   375→    if already_present:
   376→        # Stages present — check if the reason for injection still applies.
   377→        # Only auto-prune when triage was completed before (hash exists),
   378→        # all new issues have been resolved, and no triage work is in
   379→        # progress.  This avoids pruning the initial triage or a
   380→        # user-started triage session.
   381→        if last_hash and not confirmed:
   382→            new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   383→
   384→            if not new_since_triage:
   385→                # No new issues remain — prune stale stages
   386→                _prune_all_triage_stages(order)
   387→                if current_hash:
   388→                    meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   389→                    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   390→                result.pruned = True
   391→        return result
   392→
   393→    if current_hash and current_hash != last_hash:
   394→        # Distinguish "new issues appeared" from "issues were resolved".
   395→        # Only re-triage when genuinely new issues exist.
   396→        new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   397→
   398→        if new_since_triage:
   399→            # New review issues appeared — re-triage needed
   400→            result.injected = _inject_pending_triage_stages(order, plan, confirmed)
   401→        else:
   402→            # Only resolved issues changed the hash — update silently
   403→            meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   404→            plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   405→
   406→    return result

   472→def sync_create_plan_needed(

   478→    """Inject ``workflow::create-plan`` when reviews complete + objective backlog exists.
   479→

   482→    - At least one objective issue exists
   483→    - ``workflow::create-plan`` is not already in the queue
   484→    - No triage stages are pending
   485→    """
   486→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   487→    result = CreatePlanSyncResult()
   488→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   489→
   490→    if WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID in order:

   492→
   493→    # Don't inject if triage stages are pending
   494→    if any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS):

   496→

   499→        if policy.unscored_ids:

   501→        has_objective = policy.has_objective_backlog
   502→    else:

   504→        if unscored:
   505→            return result
   506→        issues = state.get("issues", {})
   507→        has_objective = any(
   508→            f.get("status") == "open"
   509→            and f.get("detector") not in _NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   510→            for f in issues.values()
   511→        )
   512→    if not has_objective:
   513→        return result

   517→    insert_at = 0
   518→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):

   521→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID)

   608→def sync_communicate_score_needed(
   609→    plan: PlanModel,
   610→    state: StateModel,
   611→    *,
   612→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   613→    scores_just_imported: bool = False,
   614→) -> CommunicateScoreSyncResult:
   615→    """Inject ``workflow::communicate-score`` when scores should be shown.
   616→
   617→    Injects when either:
   618→    - All initial subjective reviews are complete (no unscored dimensions), OR
   619→    - Scores were just imported (trusted/attested/override)
   620→
   621→    And ``workflow::communicate-score`` is not already in the queue.
   622→    Positioned after subjective items but before triage/create-plan.
   623→    """
   624→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   625→    result = CommunicateScoreSyncResult()
   626→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   627→
   628→    # Also treat legacy score-checkpoint as already-present
   629→    if WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID in order or WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID in order:
   630→        return result
   631→
   632→    # Trigger 1: scores just imported
   633→    should_inject = scores_just_imported
   634→
   635→    # Trigger 2: all initial reviews complete (no unscored dimensions)
   636→    if not should_inject:
   637→        if policy is not None:
   638→            should_inject = not policy.unscored_ids
   639→        else:
   640→            should_inject = not current_unscored_ids(state)
   641→
   642→    if not should_inject:
   643→        return result
   644→
   645→    # Insert after any subjective items, before triage/workflow/issues
   646→    insert_at = 0
   647→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   648→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX):
   649→            insert_at = i + 1
   650→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID)
   651→    result.injected = True

   282→    2. Inject stale and under-target dimension IDs when either:
   283→       a. No objective items remain (mid-cycle: append to back), OR
   284→       b. A cycle just completed (post-cycle: insert at front so subjective
   285→          review takes priority over new objective issues).
   286→    """
   287→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   288→    result = StaleDimensionSyncResult()
   289→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   290→    under_target_ids = current_under_target_ids(state)
   291→    injectable_ids = stale_ids | under_target_ids
   292→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   293→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   294→
   295→    # --- Cleanup: prune resolved subjective IDs --------------------------
   296→    # Only prune IDs that are no longer injectable and not unscored.
   297→    _prune_subjective_ids(order, keep_ids=injectable_ids | unscored_ids, pruned=result.pruned)
   298→
   299→    # --- Inject or evict stale + under-target dimensions -----------------
   300→    has_real_items = _has_objective_backlog(state, policy)
   301→    should_inject = not has_real_items or cycle_just_completed
   302→
   303→    if not should_inject:
   304→        # Mid-cycle with objective backlog: evict any stale/under-target IDs
   305→        # that are present in the queue.  They may have been grandfathered from
   306→        # the unscored phase and should not be visible until the objective
   307→        # backlog clears or a cycle completes.
   308→        to_evict = [
   309→            fid for fid in order
   310→            if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   311→            and fid in injectable_ids
   312→        ]
   313→        for fid in to_evict:
   314→            order.remove(fid)
   315→            result.pruned.append(fid)
   316→
   317→    if should_inject and injectable_ids:
   318→        to_front = cycle_just_completed and has_real_items
   319→        _inject_subjective_ids(order, plan, inject_ids=injectable_ids, to_front=to_front, injected=result.injected)
   320→
   321→    return result
   322→
   323→
   324→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   325→# Triage snapshot hash + sync
   326→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   327→
   328→def review_issue_snapshot_hash(state: StateModel) -> str:
   329→    """Hash open review issue IDs to detect changes.
   330→
   331→    Returns empty string when there are no open review issues.
   332→    """
   333→    return stale_policy_mod.review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   334→
   335→
   336→@dataclass
   337→class TriageSyncResult:
   338→    """What changed during a triage sync."""
   339→
   340→    injected: bool = False
   341→    pruned: bool = False
   342→
   343→    @property
   344→    def changes(self) -> int:
   345→        return int(self.injected) + int(self.pruned)
   346→
   347→
   348→def sync_triage_needed(
   349→    plan: PlanModel,
   350→    state: StateModel,
   351→) -> TriageSyncResult:
   352→    """Inject 4 triage stage IDs at front of queue when review issues change.
   353→
   354→    Only injects stages not already confirmed in ``epic_triage_meta``.
   355→
   356→    When stages are already present but all new issues have been resolved
   357→    since injection, auto-prunes the stale stages and updates the hash.
   358→
   359→    When issues are *resolved* (current IDs are a subset of previously
   360→    triaged IDs), the snapshot hash is updated silently — no re-triage
   361→    is needed since the user is working through the plan.
   362→    """
   363→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   364→    result = TriageSyncResult()
   365→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   366→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   367→    confirmed = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   368→
   369→    # Check if any triage stage is already in queue
   370→    already_present = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
   371→
   372→    current_hash = review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   373→    last_hash = meta.get("issue_snapshot_hash", "")
   374→
   375→    if already_present:
   376→        # Stages present — check if the reason for injection still applies.
   377→        # Only auto-prune when triage was completed before (hash exists),
   378→        # all new issues have been resolved, and no triage work is in
   379→        # progress.  This avoids pruning the initial triage or a
   380→        # user-started triage session.
   381→        if last_hash and not confirmed:
   382→            new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   383→
   384→            if not new_since_triage:
   385→                # No new issues remain — prune stale stages
   386→                _prune_all_triage_stages(order)
   387→                if current_hash:
   388→                    meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   389→                    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   390→                result.pruned = True
   391→        return result
   392→
   393→    if current_hash and current_hash != last_hash:
   394→        # Distinguish "new issues appeared" from "issues were resolved".
   395→        # Only re-triage when genuinely new issues exist.
   396→        new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   397→
   398→        if new_since_triage:
   399→            # New review issues appeared — re-triage needed
   400→            result.injected = _inject_pending_triage_stages(order, plan, confirmed)
   401→        else:
   402→            # Only resolved issues changed the hash — update silently
   403→            meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   404→            plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   405→
   406→    return result
   407→
   408→
   409→@dataclass
   410→class ScoreCheckpointSyncResult:
   411→    """What changed during a score-checkpoint sync."""
   412→
   413→    injected: bool = False
   414→
   415→    @property
   416→    def changes(self) -> int:
   417→        return int(self.injected)
   418→
   419→
   420→def sync_score_checkpoint_needed(
   421→    plan: PlanModel,
   422→    state: StateModel,
   423→    *,
   424→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   425→) -> ScoreCheckpointSyncResult:
   426→    """Inject ``workflow::score-checkpoint`` when all initial reviews complete.
   427→
   428→    Injects when:
   429→    - No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain
   430→    - ``workflow::score-checkpoint`` is not already in the queue
   431→
   432→    Positioned after subjective items but before triage/create-plan
   433→    so the user sees their updated strict score right after reviews finish.
   434→    """
   435→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   436→    result = ScoreCheckpointSyncResult()
   437→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   438→
   439→    if WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID in order:
   440→        return result
   441→
   442→    # Check that no unscored dimensions remain
   443→    if policy is not None:
   444→        if policy.unscored_ids:
   445→            return result
   446→    else:
   447→        unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   448→        if unscored:
   449→            return result
   450→
   451→    # Insert after any subjective items, before triage/workflow/issues
   452→    insert_at = 0
   453→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   454→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX):
   455→            insert_at = i + 1
   456→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID)
   457→    result.injected = True
   458→    return result
   459→
   460→
   461→@dataclass
   462→class CreatePlanSyncResult:
   463→    """What changed during a create-plan sync."""
   464→
   465→    injected: bool = False
   466→
   467→    @property
   468→    def changes(self) -> int:
   469→        return int(self.injected)
   470→
   471→
   472→def sync_create_plan_needed(
   473→    plan: PlanModel,
   474→    state: StateModel,
   475→    *,
   476→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   477→) -> CreatePlanSyncResult:
   478→    """Inject ``workflow::create-plan`` when reviews complete + objective backlog exists.
   479→
   480→    Only injects when:
   481→    - No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain
   482→    - At least one objective issue exists
   483→    - ``workflow::create-plan`` is not already in the queue
   484→    - No triage stages are pending
   485→    """
   486→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   487→    result = CreatePlanSyncResult()
   488→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   489→
   490→    if WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID in order:
   491→        return result
   492→
   493→    # Don't inject if triage stages are pending
   494→    if any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS):
   495→        return result
   496→
   497→    # Check that no unscored dimensions remain
   498→    if policy is not None:
   499→        if policy.unscored_ids:
   500→            return result
   501→        has_objective = policy.has_objective_backlog
   502→    else:
   503→        unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   504→        if unscored:
   505→            return result
   506→        issues = state.get("issues", {})
   507→        has_objective = any(
   508→            f.get("status") == "open"
   509→            and f.get("detector") not in _NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   510→            for f in issues.values()
   511→        )
   512→    if not has_objective:
   513→        return result
   514→
   515→    # Insert after any subjective/workflow items, at the end of the
   516→    # synthetic block (so create-plan comes after score-checkpoint).
   517→    insert_at = 0
   518→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   519→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(TRIAGE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(WORKFLOW_PREFIX):
   520→            insert_at = i + 1
   521→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID)
   522→    result.injected = True
   523→    return result
   524→
   525→
   526→def compute_new_issue_ids(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> set[str]:
   527→    """Return the set of open review/concerns issue IDs added since last triage.
   528→
   529→    Returns an empty set when no prior triage has recorded ``triaged_ids``.
   530→    """
   531→    return stale_policy_mod.compute_new_issue_ids(plan, state)
   532→
   533→
   534→def is_triage_stale(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> bool:
   535→    """Side-effect-free check: is triage needed?
   536→
   537→    Returns True when genuinely *new* review issues appeared since the
   538→    last triage.  Triage stage IDs being in the queue alone is not
   539→    sufficient — the new issues that triggered injection may have been
   540→    resolved since then.
   541→
   542→    When issues are merely resolved (current IDs are a subset of
   543→    previously triaged IDs), triage is NOT stale — the user is working
   544→    through the plan.
   545→    """
   546→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   547→    return stale_policy_mod.is_triage_stale(plan, state, triage_ids=TRIAGE_IDS)
   548→
   549→
   550→@dataclass
   551→class ImportScoresSyncResult:
   552→    """What changed during an import-scores sync."""
   553→
   554→    injected: bool = False
   555→
   556→    @property
   557→    def changes(self) -> int:

   559→
   560→
   561→def sync_import_scores_needed(
   562→    plan: PlanModel,
   563→    state: StateModel,
   564→    *,
   565→    assessment_mode: str | None = None,
   566→) -> ImportScoresSyncResult:
   567→    """Inject ``workflow::import-scores`` after issues-only import.
   568→
   569→    Only injects when:
   570→    - Assessment mode was ``issues_only`` (scores were skipped)
   571→    - ``workflow::import-scores`` is not already in the queue
   572→    - There are assessments in the payload that could be imported
   573→
   574→    Positioned after score-checkpoint, before create-plan.
   575→    """
   576→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   577→    result = ImportScoresSyncResult()
   578→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   579→
   580→    if WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID in order:
   581→        return result
   582→
   583→    # Only inject when scores were skipped (issues-only mode)
   584→    if assessment_mode != "issues_only":
   585→        return result
   586→
   587→    # Insert after any subjective/workflow items
   588→    insert_at = 0
   589→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   590→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(WORKFLOW_PREFIX):
   591→            insert_at = i + 1
   592→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID)
   593→    result.injected = True
   594→    return result
   595→
   596→
   597→@dataclass
   598→class CommunicateScoreSyncResult:
   599→    """What changed during a communicate-score sync."""
   600→
   601→    injected: bool = False
   602→
   603→    @property
   604→    def changes(self) -> int:
   605→        return int(self.injected)
   606→
   607→
   608→def sync_communicate_score_needed(
   609→    plan: PlanModel,
   610→    state: StateModel,
   611→    *,
   612→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   613→    scores_just_imported: bool = False,
   614→) -> CommunicateScoreSyncResult:
   615→    """Inject ``workflow::communicate-score`` when scores should be shown.
   616→
   617→    Injects when either:
   618→    - All initial subjective reviews are complete (no unscored dimensions), OR
   619→    - Scores were just imported (trusted/attested/override)
   620→
   621→    And ``workflow::communicate-score`` is not already in the queue.
   622→    Positioned after subjective items but before triage/create-plan.
   623→    """
   624→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   625→    result = CommunicateScoreSyncResult()
   626→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   627→
   628→    # Also treat legacy score-checkpoint as already-present
   629→    if WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID in order or WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID in order:
   630→        return result
   631→
   632→    # Trigger 1: scores just imported
   633→    should_inject = scores_just_imported
   634→
   635→    # Trigger 2: all initial reviews complete (no unscored dimensions)
   636→    if not should_inject:
   637→        if policy is not None:
   638→            should_inject = not policy.unscored_ids
   639→        else:
   640→            should_inject = not current_unscored_ids(state)
   641→
   642→    if not should_inject:
   643→        return result
   644→
   645→    # Insert after any subjective items, before triage/workflow/issues
   646→    insert_at = 0
   647→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   648→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX):
   649→            insert_at = i + 1
   650→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID)
   651→    result.injected = True
   652→    return result

   238→def _shallow_steps(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
   239→    """Return (cluster_name, bare_count, total_count) for clusters with steps lacking detail."""
   240→    results: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
   241→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   242→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
   243→            continue
   244→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   245→        if not steps:
   246→            continue
   247→        bare = sum(
   248→            1 for s in steps
   249→            if isinstance(s, dict) and not s.get("detail") and not s.get("issue_refs")
   250→        )
   251→        if bare > 0:
   252→            results.append((name, bare, len(steps)))
   253→    return results
   254→
   255→
   256→def _steps_with_bad_paths(plan: dict, repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]]:
   257→    """Return steps referencing file paths that don't exist on disk."""
   258→    results: list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]] = []
   259→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   260→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
   261→            continue
   262→        for i, step in enumerate(cluster.get("action_steps") or []):
   263→            if not isinstance(step, dict):
   264→                continue
   265→            detail = step.get("detail", "")
   266→            if not detail:
   267→                continue
   268→            bad: list[str] = []
   269→            for path_str in _PATH_RE.findall(detail):
   270→                p = repo_root / path_str
   271→                if p.exists():
   272→                    continue
   273→                alt_ext = _EXT_SWAPS.get(p.suffix)
   274→                if alt_ext and p.with_suffix(alt_ext).exists():
   275→                    continue
   276→                bad.append(path_str)
   277→            if bad:
   278→                results.append((name, i + 1, bad))
   279→    return results
   280→
   281→
   282→def _steps_without_effort(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
   283→    """Return (cluster_name, missing_count, total) for steps without effort tags."""
   284→    results: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
   285→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   286→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
   287→            continue
   288→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   289→        if not steps:
   290→            continue
   291→        missing = sum(
   292→            1 for s in steps
   293→            if isinstance(s, dict) and s.get("effort") not in _VALID_EFFORTS
   294→        )
   295→        if missing:
   296→            results.append((name, missing, len(steps)))
   297→    return results
   298→
   299→

   115→        print(colorize("  Run: desloppify plan triage --confirm reflect", "dim"))
   116→        print(colorize("  Or pass --attestation to auto-confirm reflect inline.", "dim"))
   117→        return False
   118→
   119→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   120→    triage_input = collect_triage_input(plan, runtime.state)
   121→    recurring = detect_recurring_patterns(
   122→        triage_input.open_issues,
   123→        triage_input.resolved_issues,
   124→    )
   125→    _by_dim, observe_dims = observe_dimension_breakdown(triage_input)
   126→    reflect_dims = sorted(set((list(recurring.keys()) if recurring else []) + observe_dims))
   127→    reflect_clusters = [
   128→        name for name in plan.get("clusters", {}) if not plan["clusters"][name].get("auto")
   129→    ]
   130→    validation_err = _validate_attestation(
   131→        attestation.strip(),
   132→        "reflect",
   133→        dimensions=reflect_dims,
   134→        cluster_names=reflect_clusters,
   135→    )
   136→    if validation_err:
   137→        print(colorize(f"  {validation_err}", "red"))
   138→        return False
   139→    stages["reflect"]["confirmed_at"] = utc_now()
   140→    stages["reflect"]["confirmed_text"] = attestation.strip()
   141→    save_plan(plan)
   142→    print(colorize("  ✓ Reflect auto-confirmed via --attestation.", "green"))
   143→    return True

   146→def _manual_clusters_or_error(plan: dict) -> list[str] | None:
   147→    manual_clusters = manual_clusters_with_issues(plan)
   148→    if manual_clusters:
   149→        return manual_clusters
   150→    any_clusters = [
   151→        name for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items() if cluster.get("issue_ids")
   152→    ]
   153→    if any_clusters:
   154→        print(colorize("  Cannot organize: only auto-clusters exist.", "red"))
   155→        print(colorize("  Create manual clusters that group issues by root cause:", "dim"))
   156→    else:

   158→    print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster create <name> --description "..."', "dim"))
   159→    print(colorize("    desloppify plan cluster add <name> <issue-patterns>", "dim"))
   160→    return None

   165→    if not gaps:

   168→    for name, missing in gaps:

   238→def _shallow_steps(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
   239→    """Return (cluster_name, bare_count, total_count) for clusters with steps lacking detail."""
   240→    results: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
   241→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   242→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
   243→            continue
   244→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   245→        if not steps:
   246→            continue
   247→        bare = sum(
   248→            1 for s in steps
   249→            if isinstance(s, dict) and not s.get("detail") and not s.get("issue_refs")
   250→        )
   251→        if bare > 0:
   252→            results.append((name, bare, len(steps)))
   253→    return results
   254→

   256→def _steps_with_bad_paths(plan: dict, repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]]:
   257→    """Return steps referencing file paths that don't exist on disk."""
   258→    results: list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]] = []
   259→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   260→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
   261→            continue
   262→        for i, step in enumerate(cluster.get("action_steps") or []):
   263→            if not isinstance(step, dict):
   264→                continue
   265→            detail = step.get("detail", "")
   266→            if not detail:
   267→                continue
   268→            bad: list[str] = []
   269→            for path_str in _PATH_RE.findall(detail):
   270→                p = repo_root / path_str
   271→                if p.exists():
   272→                    continue
   273→                alt_ext = _EXT_SWAPS.get(p.suffix)
   274→                if alt_ext and p.with_suffix(alt_ext).exists():
   275→                    continue
   276→                bad.append(path_str)
   277→            if bad:
   278→                results.append((name, i + 1, bad))
   279→    return results
   280→
   281→
   282→def _steps_without_effort(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
   283→    """Return (cluster_name, missing_count, total) for steps without effort tags."""
   284→    results: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
   285→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   286→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
   287→            continue
   288→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   289→        if not steps:
   290→            continue
   291→        missing = sum(
   292→            1 for s in steps
   293→            if isinstance(s, dict) and s.get("effort") not in _VALID_EFFORTS
   294→        )
   295→        if missing:
   296→            results.append((name, missing, len(steps)))
   297→    return results
   298→

   399→    """
   400→    results: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
   401→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   402→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
   403→            continue
   404→        for i, step in enumerate(cluster.get("action_steps") or []):
   405→            if not isinstance(step, dict):
   406→                continue
   407→            detail = step.get("detail", "")
   408→            if not detail:
   409→                continue
   410→            has_path = bool(_PATH_RE.search(detail))
   411→            if len(detail) < 80 and not has_path:
   412→                results.append((name, i + 1, step.get("title", "(no title)")))
   413→    return results
   414→
   415→
   416→def _steps_referencing_skipped_issues(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]]:
   417→    """Return steps whose issue_refs include wontfixed/skipped issues."""
   418→    wontfixed = set()
   419→    for fid, issue in plan.get("issues", {}).items():
   420→        if isinstance(issue, dict) and issue.get("status") in ("wontfix", "skipped"):
   421→            wontfixed.add(fid)
   422→    # Also check the wontfix list directly
   423→    for fid in plan.get("wontfix", {}):
   424→        wontfixed.add(fid)
   425→
   426→    if not wontfixed:
   427→        return []
   428→
   429→    results: list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]] = []
   430→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   431→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
   432→            continue
   433→        for i, step in enumerate(cluster.get("action_steps") or []):
   434→            if not isinstance(step, dict):
   435→                continue
   436→            refs = step.get("issue_refs") or []
   437→            stale = [r for r in refs if r in wontfixed]
   438→            if stale:
   439→                results.append((name, i + 1, stale))
   440→    return results
   441→
   442→
   443→def _enrich_report_or_error(report: str | None) -> str | None:
   444→    if not report:
   445→        print(colorize("  --report is required for --stage enrich.", "red"))
   446→        print(colorize("  Summarize the enrichment work you did:", "dim"))
   447→        print(colorize("  - Which clusters did you add detail/refs to?", "dim"))
   448→        print(colorize("  - Are steps specific enough for an executor with zero context?", "dim"))
   449→        print(colorize("  - Did you link issue_refs so steps auto-complete on resolve?", "dim"))
   450→        return None
   451→    if len(report) < 100:
   452→        print(colorize(f"  Report too short: {len(report)} chars (minimum 100).", "red"))
   453→        print(colorize("  Explain what enrichment you did and why steps are executor-ready.", "dim"))
   454→        return None
   455→    return report
   456→
   457→
   458→def _require_enrich_stage_for_complete(
   459→    *,
   460→    plan: dict,
   461→    meta: dict,
   462→    stages: dict,
   463→) -> bool:
   464→    if "enrich" in stages:
   465→        return True
   466→    if "organize" not in stages:
   467→        # Fall through to existing organize requirement
   468→        return _require_organize_stage_for_complete(plan=plan, meta=meta, stages=stages)
   469→
   470→    shallow = _shallow_steps(plan)
   471→    if shallow:
   472→        print(colorize("  Cannot complete: enrich stage not done.", "red"))
   473→        print(colorize(f"  {len(shallow)} cluster(s) have steps without detail or issue_refs:", "yellow"))
   474→        for name, bare, total in shallow[:5]:
   475→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {bare}/{total} steps need enrichment", "yellow"))
   476→        print(colorize(
   477→            '  Fix: desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --detail "sub-details"',
   478→            "dim",
   479→        ))
   480→        print(colorize('  Then: desloppify plan triage --stage enrich --report "..."', "dim"))
   481→    else:
   482→        print(colorize("  Cannot complete: enrich stage not recorded.", "red"))
   483→        print(colorize("  Steps look enriched. Record the stage:", "dim"))
   484→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --stage enrich --report "..."', "dim"))
   485→    return False
   486→
   487→
   488→def _auto_confirm_enrich_for_complete(
   489→    *,
   490→    plan: dict,
   491→    stages: dict,
   492→    attestation: str | None,
   493→) -> bool:
   494→    if stages.get("enrich", {}).get("confirmed_at"):
   495→        return True
   496→    if "enrich" not in stages:
   497→        return False

1→"""Shared exception tuples used across command/render flows."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→
     6→class CommandError(Exception):
     7→    """Raised by command helpers to signal a user-facing CLI error.
     8→
     9→    The CLI entrypoint catches this and prints ``message`` to stderr
    10→    before exiting with ``exit_code``.  Helpers should raise this instead
    11→    of calling ``sys.exit()`` directly so that the error path is testable
    12→    and composable.
    13→    """
    14→
    15→    def __init__(self, message: str, *, exit_code: int = 1) -> None:
    16→        self.message = message
    17→        self.exit_code = exit_code
    18→        super().__init__(message)
    19→
    20→
    21→class PacketValidationError(CommandError):
    22→    """Raised for malformed/missing review packet inputs."""
    23→
    24→
    25→class RunnerTimeoutError(CommandError):
    26→    """Raised when review batch execution fails due to timeout conditions."""
    27→
    28→
    29→class TriageValidationError(CommandError):
    30→    """Raised for invalid triage-stage attestation or workflow inputs."""
    31→
    32→
    33→PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS = (
    34→    ImportError,
    35→    AttributeError,
    36→    OSError,
    37→    ValueError,
    38→    TypeError,
    39→    KeyError,
    40→)

    26→    return bool(order & TRIAGE_IDS)
    27→
    28→def inject_triage_stages(plan: dict) -> None:
    29→    """Inject all 4 triage stage IDs into the queue (fresh start)."""
    30→    order: list[str] = plan.setdefault("queue_order", [])
    31→    existing = set(order)
    32→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    33→        if sid not in existing:
    34→            order.insert(0 if sid == TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS[0] else len(order), sid)
    35→    # Re-insert in correct order at front
    36→    for sid in reversed(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS):
    37→        if sid in order:
    38→            order.remove(sid)
    39→    insert_at = 0
    40→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    41→        order.insert(insert_at, sid)
    42→        insert_at += 1
    43→

    45→    """Purge a single triage stage ID from the queue."""
    46→    sid = f"triage::{stage_name}"
    47→    purge_ids(plan, [sid])
    48→
    49→def cascade_clear_later_confirmations(stages: dict, from_stage: str) -> list[str]:
    50→    """Clear confirmed_at/confirmed_text on stages AFTER *from_stage*. Returns cleared names."""
    51→    try:
    52→        idx = _STAGE_ORDER.index(from_stage)
    53→    except ValueError:
    54→        return []
    55→    cleared: list[str] = []
    56→    for later in _STAGE_ORDER[idx + 1:]:
    57→        if later in stages and stages[later].get("confirmed_at"):
    58→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_at", None)
    59→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_text", None)
    60→            cleared.append(later)

    45→    """Purge a single triage stage ID from the queue."""

    49→def cascade_clear_later_confirmations(stages: dict, from_stage: str) -> list[str]:
    50→    """Clear confirmed_at/confirmed_text on stages AFTER *from_stage*. Returns cleared names."""
    51→    try:
    52→        idx = _STAGE_ORDER.index(from_stage)
    53→    except ValueError:
    54→        return []
    55→    cleared: list[str] = []
    56→    for later in _STAGE_ORDER[idx + 1:]:
    57→        if later in stages and stages[later].get("confirmed_at"):
    58→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_at", None)
    59→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_text", None)
    60→            cleared.append(later)
    61→    return cleared
    62→
    63→def print_cascade_clear_feedback(cleared: list[str], stages: dict) -> None:
    64→    """Print yellow cascade-clear message with next-step guidance."""
    65→    if not cleared:
    66→        return
    67→    print(colorize(f"  Cleared confirmations on: {', '.join(cleared)}", "yellow"))
    68→    next_unconfirmed = next(
    69→        (s for s in _STAGE_ORDER if s in stages and not stages[s].get("confirmed_at")),
    70→        None,
    71→    )
    72→    if next_unconfirmed:
    73→        print(colorize(
    74→            f"  Re-confirm with: desloppify plan triage --confirm {next_unconfirmed}",
    75→            "dim",
    76→        ))
    77→
    78→def observe_dimension_breakdown(si) -> tuple[dict[str, int], list[str]]:
    79→    """Count issues per dimension from a TriageInput. Returns (by_dim, sorted_dim_names)."""
    80→    by_dim: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    81→    for _fid, f in si.open_issues.items():
    82→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
    83→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "unknown")
    84→        by_dim[dim] += 1
    85→    dim_names = sorted(by_dim, key=lambda d: (-by_dim[d], d))
    86→    return dict(by_dim), dim_names
    87→
    88→def group_issues_into_observe_batches(
    89→    si,
    90→    max_batches: int = 5,
    91→) -> list[tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict]]]:
    92→    """Group issues by dimension into batches for parallel observe.
    93→
    94→    Returns list of (dimension_names, issues_subset) tuples.
    95→    Single batch if only one dimension exists.
    96→    """
    97→    by_dim, dim_names = observe_dimension_breakdown(si)
    98→
    99→    if len(dim_names) <= 1:
   100→        return [(dim_names, dict(si.open_issues))]
   101→
   102→    # Distribute dimensions into balanced batches by issue count
   103→    num_batches = min(max_batches, len(dim_names))
   104→    batch_dims: list[list[str]] = [[] for _ in range(num_batches)]
   105→    batch_counts: list[int] = [0] * num_batches
   106→
   107→    # Greedy: assign each dimension (largest first) to the lightest batch

    50→    """Clear confirmed_at/confirmed_text on stages AFTER *from_stage*. Returns cleared names."""
    51→    try:
    52→        idx = _STAGE_ORDER.index(from_stage)
    53→    except ValueError:
    54→        return []
    55→    cleared: list[str] = []
    56→    for later in _STAGE_ORDER[idx + 1:]:
    57→        if later in stages and stages[later].get("confirmed_at"):
    58→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_at", None)
    59→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_text", None)
    60→            cleared.append(later)
    61→    return cleared
    62→
    63→def print_cascade_clear_feedback(cleared: list[str], stages: dict) -> None:
    64→    """Print yellow cascade-clear message with next-step guidance."""
    65→    if not cleared:
    66→        return
    67→    print(colorize(f"  Cleared confirmations on: {', '.join(cleared)}", "yellow"))
    68→    next_unconfirmed = next(
    69→        (s for s in _STAGE_ORDER if s in stages and not stages[s].get("confirmed_at")),
    70→        None,
    71→    )
    72→    if next_unconfirmed:
    73→        print(colorize(
    74→            f"  Re-confirm with: desloppify plan triage --confirm {next_unconfirmed}",
    75→            "dim",
    76→        ))
    77→
    78→def observe_dimension_breakdown(si) -> tuple[dict[str, int], list[str]]:
    79→    """Count issues per dimension from a TriageInput. Returns (by_dim, sorted_dim_names)."""
    80→    by_dim: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    81→    for _fid, f in si.open_issues.items():
    82→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
    83→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "unknown")
    84→        by_dim[dim] += 1
    85→    dim_names = sorted(by_dim, key=lambda d: (-by_dim[d], d))
    86→    return dict(by_dim), dim_names
    87→
    88→def group_issues_into_observe_batches(
    89→    si,
    90→    max_batches: int = 5,
    91→) -> list[tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict]]]:
    92→    """Group issues by dimension into batches for parallel observe.
    93→
    94→    Returns list of (dimension_names, issues_subset) tuples.
    95→    Single batch if only one dimension exists.
    96→    """
    97→    by_dim, dim_names = observe_dimension_breakdown(si)
    98→
    99→    if len(dim_names) <= 1:
   100→        return [(dim_names, dict(si.open_issues))]
   101→
   102→    # Distribute dimensions into balanced batches by issue count
   103→    num_batches = min(max_batches, len(dim_names))
   104→    batch_dims: list[list[str]] = [[] for _ in range(num_batches)]
   105→    batch_counts: list[int] = [0] * num_batches
   106→
   107→    # Greedy: assign each dimension (largest first) to the lightest batch
```

1→"""Stage-gate and coverage helpers for triage command handlers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     6→from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_policy import _REVIEW_DETECTORS
     7→from desloppify.engine.plan import TRIAGE_IDS
     8→
     9→
    10→def _require_triage_pending(plan: dict, *, action: str) -> bool:
    11→    """Require at least one triage stage ID to be present in queue for an action."""
    12→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    13→    if order & TRIAGE_IDS:
    14→        return True
    15→    print(colorize(f"  No triage stage in the queue — nothing to {action}.", "yellow"))
    16→    return False
    17→
    18→
    19→def _validate_stage_report(
    20→    report: str | None,
    21→    *,
    22→    stage: str,
    23→    min_chars: int,
    24→    missing_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    25→    short_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    26→) -> str | None:
    27→    """Validate staged report presence/length and print consistent guidance."""
    28→    if not report:
    29→        print(colorize(f"  --report is required for --stage {stage}.", "red"))
    30→        for line in missing_guidance or []:
    31→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    32→        return None
    33→    cleaned = report.strip()
    34→    if len(cleaned) < min_chars:
    35→        print(
    36→            colorize(
    37→                f"  Report too short: {len(cleaned)} chars (minimum {min_chars}).",
    38→                "red",
    39→            )
    40→        )
    41→        for line in short_guidance or []:
    42→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    43→        return None
    44→    return cleaned
    45→
    46→
    47→def _triage_coverage(plan: dict) -> tuple[int, int, dict]:
    48→    """Return (organized, total, clusters) for triage progress."""
    49→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    50→    all_cluster_ids: set[str] = set()
    51→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    52→        all_cluster_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    53→    queue_ids = [issue_id for issue_id in plan.get("queue_order", []) if issue_id not in TRIAGE_IDS]
    54→    organized = sum(1 for issue_id in queue_ids if issue_id in all_cluster_ids)
    55→    return organized, len(queue_ids), clusters
    56→
    57→
    58→def _unenriched_clusters(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:
    59→    """Return clusters with issues that are missing required enrichment.
    60→
    61→    Requirements:
    62→    - Every cluster needs a description and at least one action_step.
    63→    - Small clusters (< 5 issues) need at least 1 action step per issue,
    64→      so each item has a concrete plan. Large clusters (>= 5) just need
    65→      steps overall (cluster-level plan is sufficient).
    66→    """
    67→    gaps: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    68→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
    69→        if not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
    70→            continue
    71→        if cluster.get("auto"):
    72→            continue
    73→        missing: list[str] = []
    74→        if not cluster.get("description"):
    75→            missing.append("description")
    76→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
    77→        issue_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    78→        if not steps:
    79→            missing.append("action_steps")
    80→        elif issue_count < 5 and len(steps) < issue_count:
    81→            missing.append(
    82→                f"action_steps (have {len(steps)}, need >= {issue_count} for small cluster)"
    83→            )
    84→        if missing:
    85→            gaps.append((name, missing))
    86→    return gaps
    87→
    88→
    89→def _unclustered_review_issues(plan: dict, state: dict | None = None) -> list[str]:
    90→    """Return review issue IDs that aren't in any manual cluster.
    91→
    92→    When *state* is provided, uses open review/concerns issues from state
    93→    (the canonical source). Falls back to scanning queue_order for backwards
    94→    compatibility.
    95→    """
    96→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    97→    clustered_ids: set[str] = set()
    98→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    99→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
   100→            clustered_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   101→
   102→    if state is not None:
   103→        review_ids = [
   104→            fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   105→            if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in _REVIEW_DETECTORS
   106→        ]
   107→    else:
   108→        review_ids = [
   109→            fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   110→            if not fid.startswith("triage::") and not fid.startswith("workflow::")
   111→            and (fid.startswith("review::") or fid.startswith("concerns::"))
   112→        ]
   113→
   114→    return [fid for fid in review_ids if fid not in clustered_ids]
   115→

def is_subjective_issue(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    detector = item.get("detector")
    if detector in {"subjective_assessment"}:
        return True
    if detector == "holistic_review":
        return True
    return False


def is_review_issue(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    return item.get("detector") == "review"


def is_subjective_queue_item(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """True for subjective work items, including collapsed subjective clusters."""
    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
        return True
    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
        members = item.get("members", [])

## Standards

You are expected to produce **exceptional** work. The output of this triage becomes the
actual plan that an executor follows — if you are lazy, vague, or sloppy, real work gets
wasted. Concretely:

- **Read the actual source code.** Every opinion you form must come from reading the file,
  not from reading the issue title. Issues frequently exaggerate, miscount, or describe
  code that has already been fixed. Trust nothing until you verify it.
- **Have specific opinions.** "This seems like it could be an issue" is worthless. "This is
  a false positive because line 47 already uses the pattern the issue suggests" is useful.
- **Do the hard thinking.** If two issues seem related, figure out WHY. If something should
  be skipped, explain the specific reason for THIS issue, not a generic category.

   515→## SENSE-CHECK Stage Instructions
   516→
   517→This stage is handled by two parallel subagents. If you are being run as a
   518→single-subprocess fallback, perform BOTH the content and structure checks below.
   519→
   520→### Content Check (per cluster)
   521→For EVERY step in every cluster, read the actual source file and verify:
   522→1. LINE NUMBERS: Does the code at the claimed lines match the step description?
   523→2. NAMES: Do function/variable/type names in the step exist in the file?
   524→3. COUNTS: Are counts ("update the 3 imports") accurate?
   525→4. STALENESS: Is the problem still present, or already fixed?
   526→5. VAGUENESS: Could a developer with zero context execute this step?
   527→6. EFFORT TAGS: Does the tag match actual scope?
   528→7. DUPLICATES: Flag steps that duplicate work in another cluster.
   529→8. OVER-ENGINEERING: Would this change make the codebase *worse*? Flag steps that:
   530→   - Add abstractions, wrappers, or indirection for a one-time operation
   531→   - Introduce unnecessary config/feature-flags/generalization
   532→   - Make simple code harder to read for marginal benefit
   533→   - Gold-plate beyond what the issue actually requires
   534→   - Trade one smell for a worse one (e.g. fix duplication by adding a fragile base class)
   535→   Remove or simplify over-engineered steps. If the whole cluster is net-negative, say so.
   536→
   537→Fix with: `desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --detail "..." --effort <tag>`
   538→
   539→### Structure Check (global)
   540→Build a file-touch graph and check:
   541→1. SHARED FILES: Two clusters touching same file without --depends-on → add dependency
   542→2. MISSING CASCADE: Rename/remove without importer updates → add cascade step
   543→3. CIRCULAR DEPS: Flag cycles, don't add them
   544→
   545→Fix with: `desloppify plan cluster update <name> --depends-on <other>`
   546→Fix with: `desloppify plan cluster update <name> --add-step "..." --detail "..." --effort trivial --issue-refs <hash>`

Key dependency findings:
1. **package-organization should run AFTER cross-module-arch, type-safety, incomplete-migration, and design-dedup** -- because package-organization restructures engine/_plan/ which those clusters modify. If package-org runs first, subsequent changes would need different paths.
2. **type-safety and naming-and-clarity** both touch `engine/_work_queue/helpers.py` -- but different parts (is_subjective_issue vs Status enum), so no hard dependency.
3. **triage-boilerplate-dedup and incomplete-migration** both touch `stage_helpers.py` and `helpers.py` -- triage-boilerplate-dedup renames _triage_coverage, while incomplete-migration consolidates it. These should be coordinated -- **incomplete-migration should depend on triage-boilerplate-dedup** (rename first, then consolidate).
4. **type-safety and abstraction-fitness** both touch `engine/_work_queue/types.py` -- type-safety splits WorkQueueItem, abstraction-fitness removes aliases. **abstraction-fitness should depend on type-safety** for the types.py changes.
5. **cross-module-arch step 1** says DISPLAY_NAMES is in 3 places including metadata.py, but metadata.py actually imports it via metadata_legacy.py which imports from core.py. The detail is slightly misleading -- should clarify that the third "copy" is in base/subjective_dimensions.py (dict literal) and engine/_scoring/subjective/core.py (dict literal), with metadata_legacy.py importing from core.py.

    49→    mod = get_lang_hook(lang_name, "test_coverage")

    51→    if isinstance(pattern, re.Pattern):

    55→def _check_file_review_status(
    56→    abs_path: str,
    57→    cached: dict | None,
    58→    loc: int,
    59→    now: datetime,
    60→    max_age_days: int,
    61→    holistic_fresh: bool,
    62→) -> dict | None:
    63→    """Check a single file's review status. Returns an entry dict or None."""
    64→    if cached is None:
    65→        if holistic_fresh:
    66→            return None
    67→        return {
    68→            "file": abs_path,
    69→            "name": "unreviewed",
    70→            "tier": 4,
    71→            "confidence": "low",
    72→            "summary": "No design review on record — run `desloppify review --prepare`",
    73→            "detail": {"reason": "unreviewed", "loc": loc},
    74→        }
    75→
    76→    # Check if content changed since review
    77→    current_hash = _hash_file(abs_path)
    78→    if current_hash and current_hash != cached.get("content_hash", ""):
    79→        return {
    80→            "file": abs_path,
    81→            "name": "changed",
    82→            "tier": 4,
    83→            "confidence": "medium",
    84→            "summary": "File changed since last review — re-review recommended",
    85→            "detail": {"reason": "changed", "loc": loc},
    86→        }
    87→
    88→    # max_age_days == 0 means "never" — reviews don't expire
    89→    if max_age_days == 0:
    90→        return None
    91→
    92→    # Check if review is stale (age expired)
    93→    reviewed_at = cached.get("reviewed_at", "")
    94→    if reviewed_at:
    95→        try:
    96→            reviewed = datetime.fromisoformat(reviewed_at)
    97→            age_days = (now - reviewed).days
    98→            if age_days > max_age_days:
    99→                return {
   100→                    "file": abs_path,
   101→                    "name": "stale",
   102→                    "tier": 4,
   103→                    "confidence": "low",
   104→                    "summary": f"Review is stale ({age_days} days old) — re-review recommended",
   105→                    "detail": {"reason": "stale", "age_days": age_days, "loc": loc},
   106→                }
   107→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   108→            return {
   109→                "file": abs_path,
   110→                "name": "stale",
   111→                "tier": 4,
   112→                "confidence": "low",
   113→                "summary": "Review date unparseable — re-review recommended",
   114→                "detail": {"reason": "stale", "loc": loc},
   115→            }
   116→        return None
   117→
   118→    # No reviewed_at — treat as unreviewed
   119→    return {
   120→        "file": abs_path,
   121→        "name": "unreviewed",
   122→        "tier": 4,
   123→        "confidence": "low",
   124→        "summary": "No design review on record — run `desloppify review --prepare`",
   125→        "detail": {"reason": "unreviewed", "loc": loc},
   126→    }
   127→
   128→
   129→def detect_review_coverage(
   130→    files: list[str],
   131→    zone_map,
   132→    review_cache: dict,
   133→    lang_name: str,
   134→    max_age_days: int = 30,
   135→    low_value_pattern: re.Pattern | None = None,
   136→    holistic_cache: dict | None = None,
   137→    holistic_total_files: int | None = None,
   138→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   139→    """Detect production files missing reviews or carrying stale reviews."""
   140→    now = datetime.now(UTC)
   141→    entries: list[dict] = []
   142→    candidates: list[tuple[str, str, int]] = []
   143→    for filepath in files:
   144→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   145→
   146→        # Skip non-production files
   147→        if zone_map is not None:
   148→            zone = zone_map.get(filepath)
   149→            if zone.value in ("test", "generated", "vendor", "config", "script"):
   150→                continue
   151→
   152→        # Skip low-value files (language-specific + generic patterns)
   153→        if _is_low_value_file(rpath, lang_name, low_value_pattern=low_value_pattern):
   154→            continue
   155→
   156→        # Skip files below minimum LOC
   157→        abs_path = resolve_path(filepath)
   158→        content = read_file_text(abs_path)
   159→        if content is None:
   160→            continue
   161→        loc = len(content.splitlines())
   162→        if loc < MIN_REVIEW_LOC:
   163→            continue
   164→
   165→        candidates.append((abs_path, rpath, loc))
   166→
   167→    potential = len(candidates)
   168→    holistic_fresh = False
   169→    if isinstance(holistic_cache, dict) and holistic_cache:
   170→        full_sweep_included = holistic_cache.get("full_sweep_included")
   171→        if full_sweep_included is not False:
   172→            resolved_total_files = (
   173→                holistic_total_files
   174→                if isinstance(holistic_total_files, int) and holistic_total_files > 0
   175→                else potential
   176→            )
   177→            holistic_fresh = (
   178→                len(
   179→                    detect_holistic_review_staleness(
   180→                        {"holistic": holistic_cache},
   181→                        total_files=resolved_total_files,
   182→                        max_age_days=max_age_days,
   183→                    )
   184→                )
   185→                == 0
   186→            )
   187→
   188→    for abs_path, rpath, loc in candidates:
   189→        cached = review_cache.get(rpath)
   190→        entry = _check_file_review_status(
   191→            abs_path, cached, loc, now, max_age_days, holistic_fresh,
   192→        )
   193→        if entry is not None:
   194→            entries.append(entry)
   195→
   196→    return entries, potential
   197→
   198→
   199→def detect_holistic_review_staleness(
   200→    review_cache: dict,
   201→    total_files: int,
   202→    max_age_days: int = 30,
   203→) -> list[dict]:
   204→    """Detect whether a holistic codebase-wide review is needed.
   205→
   206→    Returns 0 or 1 entries:
   207→    - No holistic review on record → holistic_unreviewed
   208→    - Stale (>max_age_days) → holistic_stale
   209→    - File count drifted >20% since review → holistic_stale
   210→    """
   211→    # No production files in scope means holistic review is not applicable.
   212→    if total_files <= 0:
   213→        return []
   214→
   215→    holistic = review_cache.get("holistic")
   216→    if not holistic:
   217→        return [
   218→            {
   219→                "file": "",
   220→                "name": "holistic_unreviewed",
   221→                "tier": 4,
   222→                "confidence": "low",
   223→                "summary": "No holistic codebase review on record — run `desloppify review --prepare`",
   224→                "detail": {"reason": "unreviewed"},
   225→            }
   226→        ]
   227→
   228→    # max_age_days == 0 means "never" — holistic reviews don't expire
   229→    if max_age_days == 0:
   230→        return []
   231→
   232→    now = datetime.now(UTC)
   233→
   234→    # Check age
   235→    reviewed_at = holistic.get("reviewed_at", "")
   236→    if reviewed_at:
   237→        try:
   238→            reviewed = datetime.fromisoformat(reviewed_at)
   239→            age_days = (now - reviewed).days
   240→            if age_days > max_age_days:
   241→                return [
   242→                    {
   243→                        "file": "",
   244→                        "name": "holistic_stale",
   245→                        "tier": 4,
   246→                        "confidence": "low",
   247→                        "summary": f"Holistic review is stale ({age_days} days old) — re-review recommended",
   248→                        "detail": {"reason": "stale", "age_days": age_days},
   249→                    }
   250→                ]
   251→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   252→            return [
   253→                {
   254→                    "file": "",
   255→                    "name": "holistic_stale",
   256→                    "tier": 4,
   257→                    "confidence": "low",
   258→                    "summary": "Holistic review date unparseable — re-review recommended",
   259→                    "detail": {"reason": "stale"},
   260→                }
   261→            ]
   262→
   263→    # Check file count drift
   264→    file_count_at_review = holistic.get("file_count_at_review", 0)
   265→    if file_count_at_review > 0 and total_files > 0:
   266→        drift = abs(total_files - file_count_at_review) / file_count_at_review
   267→        if drift > 0.20:
   268→            return [
   269→                {
   270→                    "file": "",
   271→                    "name": "holistic_stale",
   272→                    "tier": 4,
   273→                    "confidence": "low",
   274→                    "summary": (
   275→                        f"Codebase changed significantly since holistic review "
   276→                        f"({file_count_at_review}→{total_files} files) — re-review recommended"
   277→                    ),
   278→                    "detail": {
   279→                        "reason": "drift",
   280→                        "old_files": file_count_at_review,
   281→                        "new_files": total_files,
   282→                    },
   283→                }
   284→            ]
   285→
   286→    return []
   287→
```

But the holistic review (which you ran) is a cross-codebase review, not a per-file one. After a holistic review runs, the `holistic_fresh` flag at line 65-66 is supposed to suppress these:

Before scan: `triaged_ids` was empty (triage was started fresh with `--start`). The hash was computed with 72 `review` + 382 `subjective_review` = 454 issues.

After scan: 382 `subjective_review` resolved → hash now covers only 72 `review` issues. Hash changed. `sync_triage_needed` at line 393: `current_hash != last_hash` → true. `_new_review_ids_since_triage` checks `_open_review_issue_ids(state) - triaged_ids`. Line 108-111: `save_plan` copies current `plan.json` to `plan.json.bak` BEFORE writing the new content. So `plan.json.bak` is the state right before the scan's final save. If the backup only has 3 stages, the enrich and sense-check stages were already gone before the scan saved.

But the scan calls `load_plan` at the start (line 301), which reads from disk. Then it mutates that plan dict in memory through all the reconciliation steps, then saves. So if enrich/sense-check were on disk when the scan started, they'd be in the loaded plan dict.

    24→def _validate_attestation(
    25→    attestation: str,
    26→    stage: str,
    27→    *,
    28→    dimensions: list[str] | None = None,
    29→    cluster_names: list[str] | None = None,
    30→) -> str | None:
    31→    """Return error message if attestation doesn't reference required data, else None."""
    32→    text = attestation.lower()
    33→
    34→    if stage == "observe":
    35→        if dimensions:
    36→            found = [d for d in dimensions if d.lower().replace("_", " ") in text or d.lower() in text]
    37→            if not found:
    38→                dim_list = ", ".join(dimensions[:6])
    39→                return f"Attestation must reference at least one dimension from the summary. Mention one of: {dim_list}"
    40→
    41→    elif stage == "reflect":
    42→        refs: list[str] = []
    43→        if dimensions:
    44→            refs.extend(d for d in dimensions if d.lower().replace("_", " ") in text or d.lower() in text)
    45→        if cluster_names:
    46→            refs.extend(n for n in cluster_names if n.lower() in text)
    47→        if not refs and (dimensions or cluster_names):
    48→            return (
    49→                f"Attestation must reference at least one dimension or cluster name.\n"
    50→                f"  Valid dimensions: {', '.join((dimensions or [])[:6])}\n"
    51→                f"  Valid clusters: {', '.join((cluster_names or [])[:6]) if cluster_names else '(none yet)'}"
    52→            )
    53→
    54→    elif stage == "organize":
    55→        if cluster_names:
    56→            found = [n for n in cluster_names if n.lower() in text]
    57→            if not found:
    58→                names = ", ".join(cluster_names[:6])
    59→                return f"Attestation must reference at least one cluster from the plan. Mention one of: {names}"
    60→
    61→    elif stage == "enrich":
    62→        if cluster_names:
    63→            found = [n for n in cluster_names if n.lower() in text]
    64→            if not found:
    65→                names = ", ".join(cluster_names[:6])
    66→                return f"Attestation must reference at least one cluster you enriched. Mention one of: {names}"
    67→
    68→    elif stage == "sense-check":
    69→        if cluster_names:
    70→            found = [n for n in cluster_names if n.lower() in text]
    71→            if not found:
    72→                names = ", ".join(cluster_names[:6])
    73→                return f"Attestation must reference at least one cluster you sense-checked. Mention one of: {names}"
    74→
    75→    return None

   684→def _cmd_confirm_stage(
   685→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   686→    *,
   687→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   688→) -> None:
   689→    """Router for ``--confirm observe/reflect/organize/enrich/sense-check``."""
   690→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   691→    confirm_stage = getattr(args, "confirm", None)
   692→    attestation = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
   693→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   694→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   695→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   696→
   697→    if confirm_stage == "observe":
   698→        _confirm_observe(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   699→    elif confirm_stage == "reflect":
   700→        _confirm_reflect(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   701→    elif confirm_stage == "organize":
   702→        _confirm_organize(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   703→    elif confirm_stage == "enrich":
   704→        _confirm_enrich(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   705→    elif confirm_stage == "sense-check":
   706→        _confirm_sense_check(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   707→
   708→
   709→MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN = _MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN
   710→validate_attestation = _validate_attestation
   711→
   712→

   714→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   715→    *,
   716→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   717→) -> None:
   718→    """Public triage confirmation entrypoint."""
   719→    _cmd_confirm_stage(args, services=services)
